title: Primitive-Call Lower Bounds for Encrypt-Mix-Encrypt and Hash-ECB-Hash
summary: Primitive-call lower bounds are known for some designs targeting n-bit SPRP security, but whether analogous bounds hold for Encrypt-Mix-Encrypt and Hash-ECB-Hash remains open.

formal_statement.body: For constructions targeting $n$-bit strong pseudorandom permutation (SPRP) security, primitive-call lower-bound results are known for certain design principles. It remains unresolved whether analogous primitive-call lower bounds apply to the Encrypt-Mix-Encrypt and Hash-ECB-Hash construction paradigms, including whether the same bounds or comparable bounds can be established for those paradigms. [S1]

scope.domain: Primitive-call complexity of strong pseudorandom permutation constructions based on the Encrypt-Mix-Encrypt and Hash-ECB-Hash paradigms.
parameters: n: target SPRP security level in bits
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the same or comparable primitive-call lower bounds known for other design principles can be established for Encrypt-Mix-Encrypt and Hash-ECB-Hash constructions.

citations.label: ZCZ – Achieving n-bit SPRP Security with a Minimal Number of Tweakable-Block-Cipher Calls

progress.summary: The source discusses primitive-call bounds for SPRP constructions under some design principles, then explicitly states that the applicability of similar results to Encrypt-Mix-Encrypt and Hash-ECB-Hash remains unclear.
citation_labels: Ritam Bhaumik et al., ZCZ – Achieving n-bit SPRP Security with a Minimal Number of Tweakable-Block-Cipher Calls
